races.title: State Senate, District 16
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Melissa Hurtado
cands.bio: Democratic state senator for District 16, first elected in 2018 (then District 14). Served on the Sanger City Council from 2016 to 2018. Earlier worked as a community organizer for public employees. Chairs the Senate Agriculture Committee. Ran for Congress in 2024 and placed fourth in the primary.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Nurses Association, SEIU Local 521 and Equality California are among her listed 2026 endorsements.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Hurtado was born or when, if ever, she moved to California; the pages only say she grew up in the Central Valley. We couldn't find her work history before 2016 beyond a note that she was a community organizer for public employees. The pages we reviewed did not document specific bills she passed or actions she took on homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, growth limits, immigration enforcement or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site describes her record in general terms, and those claims are not independently verified. No controversies turned up in the pages reviewed.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia says she grew up in the Central Valley, and her campaign site says she is the daughter of farmworkers; her birthplace isn't stated in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2018, with a 2019-2020 seat on the Budget and Fiscal Review Committee; Sanger city councilmember 2016-2018; earlier a community organizer for public employees.
qual.why: About eight years of prior legislative service, including a budget committee assignment, plus earlier local elected office, fit a job of writing law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships were not counted.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Her campaign issues page says she is opposed to the expansion of AI data centers in the Valley that strain the grid and drive up energy costs for local families.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she fought to fully fund local law enforcement and says she helped secure more than $90 million in public safety investments for Central Valley communities.

cands.name: Guillermo Asuncion Gonzalez
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Senate District 16. Born in Bakersfield. He and his family own and operate two restaurants, The Idle Spur in McFarland and Guillermo's Steakhouse in Delano. He began work in Congressman David Valadao's office during the pandemic. He has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by Republican Party of California and Reform California, per Ballotpedia (which also lists several voter-guide recommendations).
Campaign website lists endorsements from Congressman David Valadao, Congressman Vince Fong, Assemblyman Stan Ellis, and Assembly Leader Ali Macedo.
Campaign website lists endorsements from the Kern County Farm Bureau, Kern Law Enforcement Association, NFIB, Greater Bakersfield Chamber PAC, and Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association PAC.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Gonzalez holding elected office, so there is no voting record or official action to report. We couldn't find his age, education, or the specific role he held in Rep. Valadao's office. We couldn't confirm where he grew up or when he lived in California, because his campaign biography says both that he was raised in Mexico and that he worked in Bakersfield in his youth. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and the pages we had show no clear stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, immigration or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. His campaign site lists tax-cut proposals (ending the state gasoline tax and no state income tax on the first $150,000), but these are not property-tax proposals. No news coverage or controversies were found in the pages available.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Co-owner and operator of the family restaurants The Idle Spur (McFarland) and Guillermo's Steakhouse (Delano), and a staff member in Rep. David Valadao's office starting during the pandemic. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: Running a family business fits the middle band for business owners and managers. The congressional office work may add policy exposure, but his role and length of service aren't documented. He has no legislative service or budget career on record.
